title: Why Use Hashfuncs?
description: Industry-standard, non-cryptographic hashes inside DuckDB SQL — [xxHash](https://cyan4973.github.io/xxHash/), [MurmurHash3](https://github.com/aappleby/smhasher), and [RapidHash](https://github.com/Nicoshev/rapidhash). Use them for partitioning, sharding, cache keys, and probabilistic-filter inputs where speed wins and adversarial collisions don't matter. For digests, signatures, or HMAC, use the [crypto](/products/extensions/crypto) extension instead.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Hashfuncs gives you fast, deterministic 32-, 64-, and 128-bit hashes — the kind you reach for when DuckDB's built-in [`hash()`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/utility) isn't enough and a cryptographic hash is overkill.

bulletPoints.label: Hash partitioning and sharding
bulletPoints.description: Modulo a hash by the partition count to bucket rows. [`xxh3_64`](#xxh3_64) is a sensible default; [`murmurhash3_x64_128`](#murmurhash3_x64_128) is the right pick if you need to interoperate with [Cassandra](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/index.html) or [Spark](https://spark.apache.org/) hash routing.

bulletPoints.label: Probabilistic-filter inputs
bulletPoints.description: [Bloom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_filter), XOR, and Cuckoo filters need a fast `UBIGINT` hash per element. [`xxh3_64`](#xxh3_64) and [`rapidhash`](#rapidhash) feed straight into the [bitfilters](/products/extensions/bitfilters) extension.

bulletPoints.label: Stable cache and content keys
bulletPoints.description: [`xxh3_128_hex`](#xxh3_128_hex) emits the canonical 32-character hex digest used by [Python xxhash](https://pypi.org/project/xxhash/) and [xxhash-rust](https://docs.rs/xxhash-rust/latest/xxhash_rust/) — useful as a cross-language fingerprint for cache keys, dedup, and content-addressed lookups.

bulletPoints.label: Cheap deduplication
bulletPoints.description: `SELECT DISTINCT xxh3_64(...)` collapses duplicate payloads at near-RAM bandwidth. The 128-bit variants ([`xxh3_128`](#xxh3_128), [`murmurhash3_x64_128`](#murmurhash3_x64_128)) cut accidental-collision risk for very large keyspaces.

sections.title: Hashfuncs vs. crypto — picking the right extension
sections.description: These two extensions look similar but solve different problems. Pick by the threat model, not by output width.

bulletPoints.label: Use hashfuncs when speed wins
bulletPoints.description: Partitioning, sharding, deduplication, cache keys, [Bloom-filter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_filter) inputs — workloads where the adversary is randomness, not a human. [`xxh3_64`](#xxh3_64) and [`rapidhash`](#rapidhash) run roughly an order of magnitude faster than SHA-256.

bulletPoints.label: Use crypto when collisions must be hard to forge
bulletPoints.description: Digital signatures, HMAC, content-addressed storage with adversarial input, tamper-evident audit logs, password salts, secure random bytes — anything an attacker could try to break. The [crypto](/products/extensions/crypto) extension gives you BLAKE3, SHA-2, SHA-3, HMAC, and a CSPRNG.

bulletPoints.label: Don't substitute one for the other
bulletPoints.description: These hashes are explicitly **not** collision-resistant against a motivated adversary. Treating an [`xxh3_128`](#xxh3_128) like a SHA-256 digest is a security bug, not a performance optimization. Inverse: spending SHA-256 on partition routing is wasted CPU.

bulletPoints.label: They compose
bulletPoints.description: Both extensions can be loaded together. A common pattern: [`crypto`](/products/extensions/crypto) for the durable identity hash on a row, [`hashfuncs`](#xxh3_64) for the routing hash that decides which shard processes it.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: Every function is a scalar SQL function with one or two arguments — the value, and an optional seed. All families ship as upstream-faithful C/C++ implementations linked into the extension binary.

bulletPoints.label: Three families, one interface
bulletPoints.description: [xxHash](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash) ([`xxh32`](#xxh32), [`xxh64`](#xxh64), [`xxh3_64`](#xxh3_64), [`xxh3_128`](#xxh3_128), [`xxh3_128_hex`](#xxh3_128_hex)), [MurmurHash3](https://github.com/aappleby/smhasher) ([`murmurhash3_32`](#murmurhash3_32), [`murmurhash3_128`](#murmurhash3_128), [`murmurhash3_x64_128`](#murmurhash3_x64_128)), and [RapidHash](https://github.com/Nicoshev/rapidhash) ([`rapidhash`](#rapidhash)). Each takes any DuckDB scalar value as input.

bulletPoints.label: Optional seeds for independent hash spaces
bulletPoints.description: Every function has a seeded overload. Two different seeds give two uncorrelated hash spaces from the same column — useful for double-hashing in [Bloom filters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_filter) or running parallel shardings without correlation.

bulletPoints.label: Canonical 128-bit hex digest
bulletPoints.description: [`xxh3_128_hex`](#xxh3_128_hex) emits the lowercase 32-character hex form (low64 || high64) defined by the [xxHash specification](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/dev/doc/xxhash_spec.md), matching [`XXH128_canonicalFromHash`](https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash) in C, [Python xxhash](https://pypi.org/project/xxhash/), and other language bindings.

bulletPoints.label: Installs from the community repository
bulletPoints.description: Available via DuckDB's [community extensions](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/community_extensions) channel — `INSTALL hashfuncs FROM community; LOAD hashfuncs;`. No external services or secrets required.

useCases.title: Partition rows for parallel processing
useCases.description: `SELECT user_id, xxh3_64(user_id) % 16 AS partition FROM users` gives you a stable, well-distributed bucket assignment. Pair with [`CREATE TABLE AS`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_table) and [Parquet partitioning](https://duckdb.org/docs/data/parquet/overview) for shardable output.

useCases.title: Build Bloom / XOR filters at SQL speed
useCases.description: Feed [`xxh3_64`](#xxh3_64) into the [bitfilters](/products/extensions/bitfilters) extension to construct probabilistic set-membership filters in a single query — millions of keys per second on commodity hardware.

useCases.title: Cross-language content fingerprints
useCases.description: Use [`xxh3_128_hex`](#xxh3_128_hex) to produce digests that match what [Python xxhash](https://pypi.org/project/xxhash/) or [xxhash-rust](https://docs.rs/xxhash-rust/latest/xxhash_rust/) compute over the same bytes — handy for cache keys shared between SQL and application code.

useCases.title: Interoperate with Cassandra / Spark hash routing
useCases.description: [`murmurhash3_x64_128`](#murmurhash3_x64_128) matches the variant used by [Apache Cassandra](https://cassandra.apache.org/_/index.html)'s `Murmur3Partitioner` and [Apache Spark](https://spark.apache.org/)'s default hash partitioner — useful when DuckDB is downstream of a system that already routes by MurmurHash3.
